relations.note: The chthonic Turms operates under Aita’s jurisdiction, although Aita is absent.
The title Turmś Aitaś associates Turms functionally with Aita's underworld realm.
Turms appears near Aita in imagery concerning movement through the underworld.
Probable Vanth-like winged death demons attend Aita’s abduction journey.
Charun and Vanth jointly escort deceased persons in funerary processions.
Torch-bearing Vanth and hammer-bearing Charun flank a false tomb door.
Charun and Vanth attend Achilles’ killing of captives at Patroclus’ tomb.
Named Charun and Vanth stand on opposite sides of the entrance.

relations.myth: Sacrifice of Trojan captives for Patroclus
relations.note: Vanth and Charun jointly attend Achilles’ sacrifice of Trojan captives.
Menarva and Fuflunus observe Artamis carrying or seizing Esia.
Fufluns mediates Sethlans's return or admission to the divine company.
Tinia is reconstructed as Fufluns’s father by transferring the Zeus–Semele genealogy.
Turms carries, receives, or delivers the infant Fufluns to his carers.

relations.myth: Birth of Menrva from Tinia’s head
relations.note: Sethlans observes or facilitates the birth with an axe or implement.
Sethlans assists when Menrva emerges from Tinia's head.

relations.myth: Birth of Menrva from Tinia’s head
relations.note: Menrva emerges fully armed from Tinia’s skull.
Tinia gives birth to Menrva while Thanr and Ethausva assist.

relations.myth: Hercle’s adoption into the divine family
relations.note: Menrva attends with Tinia as Hercle becomes the son of Uni.
Menrva competes against Turan and Uni for Elcsntre’s judgment.
Turan attends Menrva, Laran, and the divine carers of Maris children.
Turan attends Menrva, Hercle, Epiur, and Mean during the presentation.

relations.myth: Divine colloquy before an architectural setting
relations.note: Turan appears with Menrva, Aplu, and Laran in an unexplained scene.
Turan watches while Menrva holds the infant Mariś Husrnana.
Menrva witnesses an embrace between Turan and Atunis.
Turms carries one Maris child while Menrva holds another.
Turms conducts Menrva with Uni and Turan to the judgment.
Turms appears with Menrva, Aplu, Umalee, and a speaking head.
Turms sits beside Menrva as she displays or holds Medusa's head.
Menrva and Turms each hold infants bearing forms of the name Maris.
Uni and Menrva are rival contestants before Elcsntre.
Uni and Menrva compete with Turan before Elcsntre.
Menrva supports Hercle against Uni while Tinia supports Uni.

relations.myth: Birth of Menrva from Tinia’s head
relations.note: Uni witnesses Menrva’s emergence but is not explicitly her mother.
Uni witnesses Menrva springing armed from Tinia’s head.
Sethlans stands beside Tinia, apparently prepared to open his head.
Sethlans stands with an axe, corresponding to Hephaestus in the Greek version.
Sethlans approaches the immobilized Uni to release or aid her.
Tages is Jupiter’s grandson; identification with Tinia is probable but unconfirmed.
Veltune stands armed beside Tages during the revelation of haruspicy.

relations.myth: Hercle’s adoption into the divine family
relations.note: Turan attends with Tinia during Hercle’s adoption through Uni’s nursing.
Turms stands before Tinia in an apparent heraldic audience.
Turms acts under Tinia's authority to mediate the conflict.
Turms accompanies Tinia and sometimes touches his shoulder in an unexplained scene.
Tinia stands behind Uni while Menrva supports Hercle.
Later accounts and paired images treat Uni as Tinia’s divine consort.
Uni appears beside Tinia during Menrva’s birth in the mirror tradition.
Tinia presides while Uni nurses Hercle and makes him her son.
Tinia points to the inscribed tablet authorizing or explaining Hercle’s adoption.
Some scholarship identifies Voltumna as Tinia’s title or local manifestation, but the equation remains contested.
Turms conducts Turan with Uni and Menrva to the judgment.
Turan and Turms co-attend the episode while Turms holds an infant Mariś.
Turan attends while Turms and other deities hold the Maris infants.
Turan competes with Uni and Menrva before Paris.
Uni, Menrva, and Turan compete before Elcsntre.
In some post-judgment scenes Uni and Menrva attend or honor Turan.
Turms conducts Uni with Menrva and Turan to the judgment.
Turms sometimes leads Uni and the other goddesses or mediates their encounter.

Acheron.note: Alternatively, Charun’s fellow demon coming for Admetus is identified as Acheron.

Achilles.note: Charun witnesses Achilles killing Trojan captives at Patroclus’ tomb.

Achilles.myth: Sacrifice of Trojan captives for Patroclus
Achilles.note: Vanth witnesses Achilles cutting a Trojan captive’s throat during the funeral sacrifice.

Achle.note: Tinia acts as arbiter of the fixed destiny governing Achle’s conflict.

Achviz.note: Achviz attends the lovers, sometimes carrying an alabastron.

Admetus.note: Charun comes for Admetus while Alcestis intervenes on her husband’s behalf.

Ajax.note: Charun stands present while Ajax kills or prepares to kill a captive.

Alcestis.note: Alcestis embraces Admetus or interposes herself between him and Charun.

Alpan.note: Alpan appears as a winged attendant in the Turan–Atunis assemblage.

Amamtunia.note: Amamtunia carries a Maris child beside Menrva in the Bolsena scene.
Turan and Amamtunia co-attend the episode while Amamtunia holds another Mariś.
Turms and Amamtunia flank the scene, each holding an infant Maris.

Amazons.note: A probable Vanth-type figure attends the deadly battle between Amazons and Greeks.

Aminth.myth: Aminth presents a patera over Eiasun
Aminth.note: The winged love figure gestures with a patera during Eiasun’s supplication of Fufluns.

Apa.note: Van der Meer interprets Apa as a hypostasis of infernal Tinia at Campo della Fiera.

Aphrodite Ourania.note: Clackson hypothetically derives Turan’s name from Aphrodite’s epithet Ourania.

Aplu.note: Aplu appears with Tinia and Turms in a consultation scene whose myth is lost.

Apulu.note: Apulu stands beside Fufluns and Semla; a later label also couples their names.
Apulu attends the divine assembly scene marking Sethlans's return or entrance.
Turms intervenes between Apulu and Hercle during their struggle over the hind.

Athrpa.note: Athrpa presides over a grave Turan–Atunis scene while holding a hammer.

Bacitis.note: Labeo reportedly treated their disciplines together, without narrating a personal encounter.

Calu.note: Modern scholars compare or equate Aita with the older wolf-associated death god.
An infernal Turms figure is interpreted as mediating in Calu-Aita's sphere.

Castur.note: Castur attends the scene in which Eiasun clasps Fufluns’s leg.
Castur is identified epigraphically as one of the sons of Tinia.

Catha.note: Catha occupies an adjoining divine sector; a paired cosmic relationship is scholarly inference.

Cilen.note: Cilen accompanies a Menrva figure; the identity and action remain uncertain.

Cilens.note: Cilens shares Tinia’s marginal sector in the Piacenza liver’s cosmological arrangement.

Culsu.note: Separately labeled Vanth and Culsu attend a procession near an underworld gate.

Dii superiores et involuti.note: Tinia consults hidden superior gods before releasing the destructive third thunderbolt.

Eiasun.note: Eiasun kneels and clasps Fufluns’s leg in an otherwise unknown local narrative.

Elcsntre.note: Elcsntre judges Menrva alongside Uni and Turan.
Elcsntre judges the competition among Uni, Menrva, and Turan.

Epiur.note: Hercle lifts or presents Epiur before Menrva; genealogy remains uncertain.
The child Epiur is presented to Tinia by Hercle.

Esia.note: Fuflunus witnesses Artamis carrying Esia, whose identity and fate remain disputed.

Eteocles.myth: Mutual killing of the Theban brothers
Eteocles.note: Vanth occupies the central space as Eteocles and Polynices kill one another.

Ethausva.note: Ethausva supports emerging Menrva or tends Tinia’s head.
Ethausva attends Tinia during Menrva’s birth; her precise role is obscure.

Greeks.note: A probable Vanth-type figure attends the deadly battle between Greeks and Amazons.

Helen.note: Turan touches, presents, or directs Helen toward Paris.

Hephaistos.note: Etruscan artists label Sethlans in recognizable scenes adapted from Hephaistos myths.

Hercle.note: Hercle sits with his club, awaiting or witnessing the possible divinatory rite.

Hercle.myth: Hercle’s adoption into the divine family
Hercle.note: Tinia witnesses or authorizes Hercle’s admission into Uni’s divine household.
Hercle presents the child Epiur to Tinia in an unexplained divine scene.
Turms mediates between Hercle and Apulu in their contest for the hind.

Hermione.note: Turan presides as Paris approaches Helen, who lies beside Hermione.

Hinthial Teraśiaś.note: Turmś Aitaś accompanies Tiresias's shade and enables communication across the life-death boundary.

Hydra.note: The Hydra appears among monsters in Aita’s underworld without a discrete exchange.

Laran.note: Laran appears with a drunken or supported Fufluns, Śeθlans, and Mariś.
Laran attends Menrva’s birth in a fuller mirror composition.
Laran may be the youthful armed listener during Tinia’s encounter with Lur.
Laran.source: Engraved mirror interpreted by de Grummond

Laran.note: Laran appears with youthful Tinia and Turms in a scene of unknown narrative.
Turan and Laran stand together observing the infant-centered Mariś episode.
Laran attends the scene while Turms holds one infant Maris.

Leucothea.note: Greek tradition applies Leucothea’s name to Pyrgi’s female divinity or sanctuary.

Liber.note: Roman and late-antique interpretation equated Fufluns with Liber without proving primordial identity.

Lur.note: Tinia may elicit or receive a prophecy from Lur or an oracular head.
Lur.source: Engraved mirror interpreted by de Grummond

Mae.note: Uni and Mae share one celestial compartment, but no action between them is stated.

Mantus.note: Mantus is comparatively or syncretistically identified with Aita, not securely equated.

Maris.note: One or more Maris figures attend Menrva’s birth in an expanded composition.
Turms physically holds and guards one infant labeled Maris.

Maris Halna.note: Menrva shares divine care of Maris Halna and other Maris children.

Maris Husrnana.note: Menrva holds or assists him during a vessel-centered child-care ritual.
Turms holds another Maris infant while Menrva holds Maris Husrnana.

Maris Tiusta.myth: Birth of Menrva from Tinia’s head
Maris Tiusta.note: The disputed bearded Maris Tiusta attends Menrva’s birth.

Mariś Husrnana.note: Turan attends while Menrva holds Mariś Husrnana; maternity is not established.

Mean.note: Mean crowns Hercle or attends the presentation alongside Menrva.

Mean.myth: Hercle’s adoption into the divine family
Mean.note: Mean witnesses or ratifies the adoption over which Tinia presides.
Mean appears as an attendant or personification within expanded Turan imagery.
Mean appears among named divine witnesses in some Uni-related mirror scenes.

Memnun.note: Tinia acts as arbiter of the fixed destiny leading to Memnun’s death.

Mine.note: Mine co-appears with Menrva in a composite scene lacking explanatory text.

Munθuχ.note: Munθuχ appears as an attendant within expanded Turan imagery.

Neθuns.note: Neθuns shares an interior liver field with Tinia; their association is unexplained.

Odysseus.note: Odysseus receives Teiresias within Aita’s implied jurisdiction; Aita remains absent.
Vanth shields Odysseus’ escape from Polyphemus’ stones with her mantle and sword.

Panes.note: The Panes and Vertumnus are rival suitors, though no direct confrontation is narrated.

Paris.note: Turan oversees or actively facilitates Paris’s approach to Helen.
Paris judges Turan against Uni and Menrva; Turan apparently wins.

Patroclus.note: Charun attends the sacrifice performed at Patroclus’ tomb or for his shade.

Peirithoos.note: Peirithoos appears as a subject or prisoner in Aita’s realm.

Penthesilea.note: Charun receives or confronts the shade of Penthesilea with another Amazon.

Pherse.note: Menrva accompanies and protects Pherse in Etruscan Medusa-cycle images.

Phersipnai.note: Turms appears in infernal imagery associated with Phersipnai's movement between realms.

Polynices.myth: Mutual killing of the Theban brothers
Polynices.note: Vanth occupies the central space as Polynices and Eteocles kill one another.

Pultuce.note: Pultuce is identified epigraphically as one of the sons of Tinia.

Rath.note: The genitives of Turms and Rath occur together on a possible joint dedication.
Veltune appears with a figure or location ambiguously associated with Rath.

Raθlθ.note: Raθlθ stands opposite Veltune during the possible Tages’ liver consultation.

Satyrs.note: The Satyrs and Vertumnus are rival suitors, though no direct confrontation is narrated.

Selvans.note: Selvans stands beside Fufluns in the Liver’s reconstructed terrestrial divine sequence.

Semla.note: Semla is understood as Fufluns’s mother through the adopted Dionysian genealogy.
Adult Fufluns embraces his mother; proposed resurrection interpretations remain unproved.
Semla attends the divine assembly scene involving Sethlans and Fufluns.

Shade of Patroclus.myth: Sacrifice of Trojan captives for Patroclus
Shade of Patroclus.note: Vanth attends the blood sacrifice performed for the wounded shade of Patroclus.

Sime.note: The named satyr attends the embrace between Fufluns and Areatha.

Soranus.note: Soranus is comparatively or syncretistically identified with Aita, not securely equated.

Svutaf.note: Svutaf guides Vesuna’s gaze toward reflective liquid while Fufluns officiates.

Tarchon.note: Tages rebukes Tarchon’s incredulity and answers his questions about sacred doctrine.
The possible Tages examines a liver beside Tarchon in a disputed identification.

Teiresias.note: Teiresias’s shade appears under Aita’s implied sovereignty; they do not meet.

Thalna.myth: Birth of Menrva from Tinia’s head
Thalna.note: Thalna assists or attends Menrva’s birth from Tinia.
Thalna assists Tinia during Menrva’s emergence in regional mirror versions.
Turan apparently places a crown upon Thalna.
Thalna attends Turan and Atunis on related mirrors.
Thalna or Thanr appears among the divine witnesses in some nursing mirrors.

Thanr.note: Thanr participates in Menrva’s delivery from Tinia’s head.
Thanr assists or attends while Menrva emerges from Tinia’s head.

Thesan.note: A solar or dawn chariot above the scene is commonly interpreted as Thesan.
Thesan appeals to Tinia concerning her doomed son Memnun.

Theseus.note: Theseus appears as a subject or prisoner in Aita’s realm.

Thethis.note: Thethis appeals alongside Thesan while Tinia arbitrates their sons’ fixed destinies.

Thevrumines.note: Menrva and the bull-human Thevrumines share a recombined Cretan mythic scene.

Thufltha.note: Thufltha is compounded or juxtaposed with Tinia, possibly as a punitive power.

Troilus.note: Vanth holds a tall torch beside Troilus after his beheading by Achilles.

Trojan captives.myth: Sacrifice of Trojan captives for Patroclus
Trojan captives.note: Vanth witnesses the captives’ ritual throat-cutting but does not kill them.

Tuchulcha.note: Charun and a demon possibly identified as Tuchulcha jointly come for Admetus.

Turnu.note: Turnu is commonly reconstructed as Turan’s son from repeated iconographic association.
Turnu accompanies Turan and uses an iynx to facilitate or foretell desire.

Tusna.note: The named swan Tusna appears beside Turan and Atunis.

Twelve dii consentes.note: Tinia consults twelve gods before releasing the second, more serious thunderbolt.

Umalee.note: The uncertain Umalee appears with Menrva in an unrecoverable divinatory narrative.

Vegoia.note: Their prophetic corpora are cited together as overlapping authorities without a personal encounter.

Vei.note: Vei received a distinct but complementary cult within Uni’s precinct at Kainua.

Veiovis.note: Roman and modern systematizations tentatively equate chthonic Tinia with Veiovis or Vedius.

Veltune.note: Veltune witnesses or frames the possible Tages’ haruspical consultation.

Vesuna.myth: Fufluns and Vesuna perform bowl divination
Vesuna.note: Vesuna turns toward a vessel while Fufluns handles wine implements in a possible divination.

Vile.note: Vile co-appears with Menrva in the composite Cretan mirror scene.

Zipna.note: Zipna attends Turan in toilette and Turan–Atunis scenes.

the Lasa figures.note: Winged Lasa spirits accompany Turan’s erotic, domestic, and adornment scenes.

Śeθlans.note: Fufluns intoxicates and escorts the smith god back to Olympus.

Śuri.note: Aita’s equation with Śuri is a contested modern reconstruction without direct ancient testimony.
